questions.question_text: In South Dakota, the entry-level real estate license is called a:
questions.explanation: South Dakota calls its entry-level license broker associate; the supervising license is responsible broker. Most states use salesperson and broker for the same two rungs, which makes this terminology a common source of exam confusion.

questions.question_text: Which South Dakota real estate license requires NO education or examination?
questions.explanation: A residential rental agent may be licensed with no education and no examination — just an approved application and the $60 fee (ARSD 20:69:14.01:05). The agent works under a broker or property manager and still owes 12 hours of continuing education each cycle.

questions.question_text: A person wants to manage rental properties in South Dakota. How many hours of education are required for the property management license?
questions.explanation: A property manager needs 40 hours of fundamentals-of-property-management education completed within the two years before applying (ARSD 20:69:14:02.01), plus a passing exam. A real estate broker may add the property manager license without an examination.

questions.question_text: To become a responsible broker in South Dakota, what is the minimum period of active broker associate status required?
questions.explanation: A responsible broker applicant must have served actively for two years as a licensed salesperson or broker associate, or a combination of the two, and complete 24 additional class hours (SDCL 36-21A-31).

questions.question_text: A broker associate in South Dakota wants to upgrade to responsible broker. What additional course must they complete?
questions.explanation: Twenty-four class hours beyond the broker associate level are required, on top of two years of active service (SDCL 36-21A-31). The commission may license conditionally if the applicant finishes those hours within six months.

questions.question_text: A broker associate candidate passes the state exam on March 1. By what date must they submit their license application?
questions.explanation: The application and all required documents are due within 60 days of the notice that the applicant passed (SDCL 36-21A-36.1). Miss it and the registration and every right from the passing score are canceled.

questions.question_text: How many classroom hours of pre-licensing education must a South Dakota broker associate candidate complete?
questions.explanation: A broker associate applicant must complete 116 class hours in a commission-approved course (SDCL 36-21A-30.1). The license application must also be filed within two years of finishing the pre-licensing course.

questions.question_text: A broker associate candidate is preparing their budget. What is the non-refundable application fee?
questions.explanation: The application fee for brokers and broker associates is $225 (ARSD 20:69:03:10). Budget separately for the PSI exam registration, which the commission lists at $105, and for the DCI and FBI fingerprint fees the applicant pays.

questions.question_text: Which must a broker associate obtain BEFORE receiving their South Dakota license?
questions.explanation: Proof of E&O coverage must be on file before an active license is issued (SDCL 36-21A-119). Applicants must also clear DCI and FBI fingerprint background checks before licensure. South Dakota requires no surety bond.

questions.question_text: What minimum passing score is required on both the national and state portions of the SD real estate exam?
questions.explanation: Both portions require a score of 75 (ARSD 20:69:03:07). The national portion is 90 items in 150 minutes and the state portion is 52 items in 120 minutes; each is scored on its own, so only a failed portion is retaken.

questions.question_text: A new broker associate must complete how many total hours of postlicensing education?
questions.explanation: New broker associates owe 60 hours of postlicensing education — 30 in the first active license cycle and 30 in the second (SDCL 36-21A-30.2). Those hours are continuing education, not an extra layer: they count toward the renewal requirement.

questions.question_text: How many continuing education hours must a South Dakota broker associate complete per renewal cycle?
questions.explanation: Brokers, broker associates, salespersons, auctioneers, and property managers each need 24 hours every two years, at least 12 of them in required subject areas (SDCL 36-21A-62). Residential rental agents need only 12 hours.

questions.question_text: A licensee forgets to renew by the November 30 deadline. What late penalty applies?
questions.explanation: The late fee is $20 for each month or part of a month past November 30, climbing to $140 by June (ARSD 20:69:03:27). No late application is accepted after June 30, and the licensee may not practice until the commission renews the license.

questions.question_text: Of the 24 hours of CE required per cycle, how many must be in mandatory subject areas?
questions.explanation: At least 12 of the 24 hours must come from the required list: ethics, legislative issues, license law administration, brokerage, fair housing, environmental issues, antitrust, the ADA, and property management (ARSD 20:69:11:02).

questions.question_text: On what date do all South Dakota real estate licenses expire?
questions.explanation: Renewal applications are due by November 30, but the license itself does not expire until December 31 if the licensee fails to register (SDCL 36-21A-61). Missing November 30 triggers a monthly late fee, not immediate expiration.
